reasons: Deterministic workflow with a bounded agent for sanctions screening fits the known sequence; agent is bounded at 5 turns with a single tool.

Human approval gates the consequential write (approve-onboard) on the high-risk path after the final content producer; standard-risk path is an internal reversible write, so no routine approval is defensible.
Model tiers are reasonable: qwen3.8-flash for classification, qwen3.7-plus for identity verification/extraction, qwen3.8-max for the multi-step sanctions search agent.
Products are internationally available: FC, AI Guardrails (Singapore), AgentRun code runtime (Singapore), CloudFlow with WaitForCustomCallback for human review.

defects: The standard-risk path writes the customer record without human approval; while internal writes may not need default approval, onboarding approval is a consequential decide that arguably warrants review on all paths, not just high-risk.
The guard node screens inbound payload but there is no explicit guard on the screen-agent's web_search results (untrusted external content) before it influences the risk decision.
assess-risk uses qwen3.8-flash for a decision that determines compliance routing; a mid-tier model might be more reliable for this consequential classification.
No explicit handling for guard-rejected input (what happens if AI Guardrails flags the payload?).
